heading.en: Idli batter, curd and tired muscles
heading.kn: ಇಡ್ಲಿ ಹಿಟ್ಟು, ಮೊಸರು ಮತ್ತು ದಣಿದ ಸ್ನಾಯುಗಳು

hook.en: Idli batter rises overnight, milk turns to curd, and your legs ache after a long run. All three are about what cells do with pyruvic acid when oxygen is short.
hook.kn: ಇಡ್ಲಿ ಹಿಟ್ಟು ರಾತ್ರಿ ಉಬ್ಬುತ್ತದೆ, ಹಾಲು ಮೊಸರಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ದೂರ ಓಡಿದ ಮೇಲೆ ಕಾಲು ನೋಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಇದ್ದಾಗ ಜೀವಕೋಶಗಳು ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವನ್ನು ಏನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂಬುದೇ ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ.

objectives.en: Describe alcoholic and lactic acid fermentation.
Explain why fermentation releases little energy.

narration.en: Idli batter rises overnight, milk turns to curd, and your legs ache after a long run. All three are about what cells do with pyruvic acid when oxygen is short.
narration.kn: ಇಡ್ಲಿ ಹಿಟ್ಟು ರಾತ್ರಿ ಉಬ್ಬುತ್ತದೆ, ಹಾಲು ಮೊಸರಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ದೂರ ಓಡಿದ ಮೇಲೆ ಕಾಲು ನೋಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಇದ್ದಾಗ ಜೀವಕೋಶಗಳು ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವನ್ನು ಏನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂಬುದೇ ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ.

body.en: Pyruvic acid, the key product of glycolysis, has three major fates: lactic acid fermentation, alcoholic fermentation and aerobic respiration. Fermentation takes place under anaerobic conditions in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes. In alcoholic fermentation by yeast, pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase convert pyruvic acid to CO₂ and ethanol. Some organisms, such as lactic acid bacteria, and animal muscle cells during vigorous exercise when oxygen is inadequate, reduce pyruvic acid to lactic acid using lactate dehydrogenase. In both, NADH + H⁺ is reoxidised to NAD⁺, which lets glycolysis continue.

points.en: Muscle and lactic acid bacteria: pyruvate → lactic acid.

narration.kn: ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕರಹಿತ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯೀಸ್ಟ್ ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವನ್ನು ಎಥನಾಲ್ ಮತ್ತು CO₂ ಆಗಿ ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸ್ನಾಯುಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಅದನ್ನು ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವಾಗಿ ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: Let us draw where pyruvic acid goes with and without oxygen.

say.en: Pyruvic acid, the end product of glycolysis, has three possible fates, depending on the organism and on oxygen.
Without oxygen, muscles and lactic acid bacteria make lactic acid; yeast makes ethanol and CO₂. With oxygen, pyruvate is fully oxidised.
In both fermentations the NADH from glycolysis is oxidised back to NAD⁺, so glycolysis can keep running.
Fermentation releases less than seven per cent of the energy in glucose, and yeast poisons itself when alcohol reaches about 13 per cent.

body.en: In both lactic acid and alcohol fermentation not much energy is released: less than 7% of the energy in glucose is released, and not all of it is trapped as ATP. The processes are also hazardous: the products are either acid or alcohol. Yeasts poison themselves to death when the alcohol concentration reaches about 13%. For complete oxidation of glucose to CO₂ and H₂O, organisms use the Krebs cycle (aerobic respiration), which needs O₂.

points.en: Less than 7% of glucose energy is released.
Net ATP in fermentation = 2 per glucose (from glycolysis).

problem.en: A yeast culture fermenting glucose stops producing CO₂ after some days although sugar is still left. Suggest why, and state how much ATP yeast gains per glucose in fermentation.

steps.en: Fermentation products are hazardous; ethanol builds up in the medium.
At about 13% alcohol, yeasts poison themselves and stop.
Only glycolysis yields ATP in fermentation: net 2 ATP per glucose.

answer.en: Alcohol reached about 13% and killed the yeast; net 2 ATP per glucose

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A yeast culture fermenting glucose stops producing CO₂ after some days although sugar is still left. Suggest why, and state how much ATP yeast gains per glucose in fermentation.

body.en: Yeast needs two enzymes: first remove CO₂ (decarboxylase), then reduce to alcohol (alcohol dehydrogenase). Muscle needs one: lactate dehydrogenase.

narration.en: Fermentation enzymes. Yeast needs two enzymes: first remove CO₂ (decarboxylase), then reduce to alcohol (alcohol dehydrogenase). Muscle needs one: lactate dehydrogenase.

mnemonic.en: "Yeast: De-carb then Drink; Muscle: Lactate only"
